{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Implement the NIO stack as a deploy.properties-controlled option with backward-compatible default behavior when the toggle is absent.",
    "Implement WebSocket support using Mule's existing transport and connector abstractions so WebSocket endpoints can participate in normal Mule flows and lifecycle management.",
    "Represent Registry pairing as instance-level configuration containing the registry key, with secure handling and validation during startup or deployment.",
    "Integrate endpoint registration and management through the existing Registry client/API abstractions rather than introducing a separate endpoint-management subsystem.",
    "Implement dynamic lookup as a reusable flow component that resolves an endpoint at runtime and supports Registry-backed dynamic endpoint resolution.",
    "Implement throttling as a policy/interceptor applied at Mule flow endpoints, with configurable limits and predictable rejection behavior.",
    "Use existing Mule event and transaction-context facilities to include custom business event identifiers and transaction IDs in application log output.",
    "Upgrade the MVEL dependency to version 2.1.8 while preserving existing expression and DataMapper compatibility.",
    "Provide JDBC configuration and connection support for Oracle, PostgreSQL, Sybase, Microsoft SQL Server, and DB2, while retaining the existing MySQL support.",
    "Implement optional SQL query logging through DEBUG-level logging, with logging disabled by default and parameters handled in a way that avoids exposing sensitive values unnecessarily.",
    "Use unit, integration, compatibility, and regression tests around each feature, including representative database and Registry integration scenarios.",
    "Assume the implementation will follow the existing Mule 3.5.0 architecture, build system, configuration conventions, and supported Java runtime."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The referenced internal Registry and Dynamic Router specifications are available to the developer and their APIs are stable enough for implementation; no Registry server-side feature development is included.",
    "Registry authentication, licensing, endpoint-management APIs, and throttling-policy APIs already exist or are supplied by compatible client libraries.",
    "The increment is implemented in the existing Mule 3.5.0 codebase and does not require a major framework migration.",
    "WebSocket protocol support is limited to the components and flow semantics required by the user stories; advanced features such as clustering semantics, protocol extensions, and browser-specific compatibility work are excluded.",
    "Database vendor testing can use available development or containerized instances; procurement, administration, and production deployment of database servers are excluded.",
    "Vendor JDBC drivers are either already available through approved dependencies or can be referenced without redistributing proprietary drivers.",
    "MySQL support is treated as complete and only receives regression coverage.",
    "Backward compatibility is required for existing deployments, configurations, flows, logging behavior, and database connectors.",
    "Security review is limited to implementation-level checks such as protecting registry keys in configuration and avoiding unsafe query-parameter logging; a separate formal security audit is excluded.",
    "Documentation covers configuration, deployment properties, flow usage, supported databases, logging controls, and operational behavior.",
    "Effort includes coding, code review preparation, local troubleshooting, automated tests, and developer-level documentation, but excludes project management, release management by other teams, and elapsed waiting time for external environments.",
    "No substantial undocumented defects in the existing Mule transport, Registry client, JDBC, or logging infrastructure are discovered."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Requirements and architecture analysis",
      "activity_description": "Review the user stories, existing Mule 3.5.0 architecture, transport and connector abstractions, Registry integration points, logging framework, dependency management, and the referenced detailed specifications. Produce an implementation plan and identify compatibility constraints.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "NIO toggle and WebSocket components",
      "activity_description": "Add deploy.properties configuration for enabling the NIO stack, wire the setting into server and transport initialization, implement or integrate WebSocket inbound and outbound flow components, handle lifecycle and error behavior, and add component configuration support.",
      "most_likely_effort": 64
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "Registry account pairing and endpoint management",
      "activity_description": "Add registry-key configuration for an ESB instance, validate and initialize the Registry pairing, register HTTP endpoints for deployed applications, synchronize endpoint lifecycle changes, handle failures and retries, and preserve secure configuration behavior.",
      "most_likely_effort": 80
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "Dynamic lookup component",
      "activity_description": "Implement the dynamic lookup or dynamic router component, including runtime endpoint resolution, Registry-backed resolution, flow message and metadata handling, timeout/error behavior, and configuration validation.",
      "most_likely_effort": 56
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "Endpoint throttling policies",
      "activity_description": "Integrate Registry throttling policies with Mule flow endpoints, implement policy retrieval and enforcement, define behavior when limits are exceeded or the Registry is unavailable, and expose operational configuration and diagnostics.",
      "most_likely_effort": 72
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "Business event and transaction ID logging",
      "activity_description": "Extend Mule logging context and relevant log formatters so custom business event identifiers and transaction IDs are emitted during development, while maintaining compatibility with existing logging configuration and avoiding unnecessary production overhead.",
      "most_likely_effort": 32
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "MVEL dependency upgrade",
      "activity_description": "Update dependency declarations to MVEL 2.1.8, resolve transitive dependency or packaging issues, verify DataMapper and existing MVEL expression behavior, and update dependency-related tests or metadata.",
      "most_likely_effort": 16
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "JDBC support for prioritized relational databases",
      "activity_description": "Add or complete low-configuration JDBC support for Oracle, PostgreSQL, Sybase, Microsoft SQL Server, and DB2, including vendor detection/configuration defaults, connection validation, dialect or metadata differences, error handling, and regression preservation for MySQL.",
      "most_likely_effort": 72
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "Optional JDBC query logging",
      "activity_description": "Add configurable DEBUG-level logging of SQL queries executed through Mule JDBC facilities, integrate with the existing logging framework, support safe enablement and disablement, and cover prepared statements and representative error paths.",
      "most_likely_effort": 40
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "Automated integration and regression testing",
      "activity_description": "Create and execute unit, component, and integration tests covering NIO/WebSocket behavior, Registry pairing and endpoint lifecycle, dynamic lookup, throttling, event logging, MVEL compatibility, all targeted JDBC vendors where environments are available, query logging, configuration defaults, and backward compatibility.",
      "most_likely_effort": 64
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A11",
      "activity_name": "Documentation and usage examples",
      "activity_description": "Document deploy.properties settings, WebSocket flow configuration, Registry pairing, endpoint management, dynamic lookup, throttling, event and SQL logging, supported JDBC databases, upgrade notes, and representative configuration or flow examples.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A12",
      "activity_name": "Build, packaging, and release verification",
      "activity_description": "Update build metadata and packaged dependencies, verify clean and incremental builds, run the relevant test suites, check installation and upgrade behavior, inspect generated artifacts, and prepare the increment for review or release.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 568
  }
}

technical_and_design_decisions: Implement the NIO stack as a deploy.properties-controlled option with backward-compatible default behavior when the toggle is absent.
Implement WebSocket support using Mule's existing transport and connector abstractions so WebSocket endpoints can participate in normal Mule flows and lifecycle management.
Represent Registry pairing as instance-level configuration containing the registry key, with secure handling and validation during startup or deployment.
Integrate endpoint registration and management through the existing Registry client/API abstractions rather than introducing a separate endpoint-management subsystem.
Implement dynamic lookup as a reusable flow component that resolves an endpoint at runtime and supports Registry-backed dynamic endpoint resolution.
Implement throttling as a policy/interceptor applied at Mule flow endpoints, with configurable limits and predictable rejection behavior.
Use existing Mule event and transaction-context facilities to include custom business event identifiers and transaction IDs in application log output.
Upgrade the MVEL dependency to version 2.1.8 while preserving existing expression and DataMapper compatibility.
Provide JDBC configuration and connection support for Oracle, PostgreSQL, Sybase, Microsoft SQL Server, and DB2, while retaining the existing MySQL support.
Implement optional SQL query logging through DEBUG-level logging, with logging disabled by default and parameters handled in a way that avoids exposing sensitive values unnecessarily.
Use unit, integration, compatibility, and regression tests around each feature, including representative database and Registry integration scenarios.
Assume the implementation will follow the existing Mule 3.5.0 architecture, build system, configuration conventions, and supported Java runtime.
assumptions: The referenced internal Registry and Dynamic Router specifications are available to the developer and their APIs are stable enough for implementation; no Registry server-side feature development is included.
Registry authentication, licensing, endpoint-management APIs, and throttling-policy APIs already exist or are supplied by compatible client libraries.
The increment is implemented in the existing Mule 3.5.0 codebase and does not require a major framework migration.

WebSocket protocol support is limited to the components and flow semantics required by the user stories; advanced features such as clustering semantics, protocol extensions, and browser-specific compatibility work are excluded.
Database vendor testing can use available development or containerized instances; procurement, administration, and production deployment of database servers are excluded.
Vendor JDBC drivers are either already available through approved dependencies or can be referenced without redistributing proprietary drivers.
MySQL support is treated as complete and only receives regression coverage.
Backward compatibility is required for existing deployments, configurations, flows, logging behavior, and database connectors.
Security review is limited to implementation-level checks such as protecting registry keys in configuration and avoiding unsafe query-parameter logging; a separate formal security audit is excluded.
Documentation covers configuration, deployment properties, flow usage, supported databases, logging controls, and operational behavior.

Effort includes coding, code review preparation, local troubleshooting, automated tests, and developer-level documentation, but excludes project management, release management by other teams, and elapsed waiting time for external environments.
No substantial undocumented defects in the existing Mule transport, Registry client, JDBC, or logging infrastructure are discovered.
